mainTopic: What handing a bride over to the husband's messengers (מסירה) accomplishes: inheritance, כתובה, תרומה, and her punishment for adultery.
overview: The עמוד opens with the end of the משנה. A bride moves into her husband's authority once her father, or his messengers, hand her over to the husband's messengers. If the father's side still goes along with her, she stays under her father. The גמרא explains that the word 'לעולם' rejects an earlier ruling (משנה ראשונה) that let a bride eat תרומה once the wedding date passed. Then אמוראים argue about what the handing over (מסירה) accomplishes. רב says it counts for everything except תרומה, and רב אסי, רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא say even for תרומה. שמואל says it counts for inheritance, and ריש לקיש says for her כתובה, which רבינא explains as her later כתובה being a מנה. A ברייתא then says the handing over works for inheritance, but she may eat תרומה only after the חופה, and this refutes everyone who allowed תרומה. רב אשי settles a contradiction inside that ברייתא: with nothing said, her courtyard means lodging and his courtyard means marriage. Finally, a ברייתא rules that a bride handed to the husband's messengers who sins gets חנק, learned from the words 'בית אביה'.

steps.title: The משנה: when the handing over moves her to the husband
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rule and gives cases. If the father, or the father's messengers, hand her to the husband's messengers, she is under the husband. If the father's side still goes along with her, she stays under the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: (She stays under her father until she enters) the husband's authority for marriage. If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers, she is under the husband's authority. If the father went along with the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers went along with the husband's messengers, she is still under the father's authority. If the father's messengers handed her over to the husband's messengers, she is under the husband's authority.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It explains exactly when a bride leaves her father's authority and comes under her husband's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is a real handing over (מסירה). As long as the father or his people still travel with her, the father has not let go, so she is still his. Once his side fully hands her to the husband's side, she belongs to the husband's authority.

keyTerms.meaning: The father's authority over his daughter
The husband's authority over his wife
The final stage of marriage, the חופה
Handed over
The husband's messengers who come to bring the bride

steps.whatToRemember: Only a full handing over to the husband's messengers moves her to the husband. If the father's side still goes along with her, she stays with the father.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bride moves from her father's authority to her husband's once the father or his messengers fully hand her to the husband's messengers. If the father's side still accompanies her, she stays under her father.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'always'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'לעולם' (always) in the משנה is meant to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'always' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking about one word in the משנה. This question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said she is 'always' under her father until she reaches the husband's authority. The word 'always' seems extra, so the גמרא wants to know what case it is meant to rule out.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Always

phrases.english: Gemara: What does 'always' come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה's opening rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'לעולם' is meant to exclude.

steps.title: 'Always' rules out the earlier version of the law
steps.stepSummary: 'Always' rejects the משנה ראשונה. That earlier ruling said that once the wedding date arrived, a bride could already eat from the groom's food and eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to rule out the earlier version of the משנה. As we learned: if the set time came and they were not yet married, the brides eat from his food and eat תרומה. So our משנה teaches us 'always': she stays under her father until the actual marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The word 'always' tells us we do not follow an older ruling that treated a bride as married once the wedding date passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the earlier ruling, simply reaching the wedding date was enough for her to be supported by the groom and to eat תרומה. Our משנה says 'always' to show that this ruling was dropped. Nothing changes until she actually enters the husband's authority.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out
An earlier ruling that was later changed
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
It teaches us

phrases.english: To rule out the earlier version of the Mishnah.
As we learned:
If the set time came and they were not married,
they eat from his food
and they eat תרומה.
phrases.notes: The groom here is a כהן, so his wife may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: It teaches us: 'always.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'לעולם'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לעולם' rejects the משנה ראשונה, which let a bride eat from the groom and eat תרומה once the wedding date arrived.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Always' means the wedding date by itself changes nothing. She stays under her father until she actually enters the husband's authority.

steps.title: רב: handing over counts for everything except תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's handing-over case. רב says it moves her to the husband in every way, but she still may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers, she is under the husband's authority,' and so on. רב said: her handing over counts for everything, except for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the handing-over case in the משנה. רב gives a limit: the handing over works for every matter except eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For things like the father's rights, the handing over makes her the husband's. But for eating תרומה, רב says she must wait until the actual חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her being handed over
Except for
And so on (the quote continues)

phrases.english: 'If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers,
she is under the husband's authority,' and so on.
רב said:
Her handing over counts for everything,
except for תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מְסִירָתָהּ לַכֹּל, חוּץ מִתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה's handing-over case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מסירה to the husband's messengers moves her into the husband's authority for everything except eating תרומה.

steps.title: רב אסי: even for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי disagrees with רב. He holds that the handing over is enough even for eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: it counts even for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives the opposing view. Once she is handed over, she may already eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats תרומה as an exception, but רב אסי makes no exception at all. For him, the handing over works like full marriage in every way.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: And רב אסי said:
Even for תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מסירה lets her eat תרומה too.

steps.title: Objection to רב אסי from 'until she enters the חופה'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא (or חייא בר רב) challenges רב אסי from a source that says she stays under her father until she enters the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא objected to רב אסי, and some say it was חייא בר רב who objected to רב אסי: 'She is always under her father's authority until she enters the חופה!'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks רב אסי's view using a teaching that names the חופה as the moment she leaves her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she stays under her father until the חופה, then the handing over alone should not be enough. That seems to prove רב אסי wrong about תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
And some say
The wedding canopy, which completes the marriage

phrases.english: רב הונא raised an objection to רב אסי,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and some say it was חייא בר רב who objected to רב אסי:
She is always under her father's authority
until she enters the חופה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's view that מסירה allows תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source names the חופה as the point she leaves her father, so the handing over alone should not be enough.

steps.title: רב defends רב אסי: handing over is like entering the חופה
steps.stepSummary: רב rebukes the questioners: you cannot refute someone from a source that can be read either way. רב אסי can explain that the handing over is the same as entering the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to them: Didn't I tell you not to follow a source that can be turned the other way? He can answer you: her handing over is the same as her entering the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב himself defends רב אסי, even though he disagrees with him. He shows the objection does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חופה' in the source can be read to include the handing over. So this source does not prove anything against רב אסי. The question is settled later by a ברייתא (steps 13-16).

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, a reading that can be turned around
To answer, to explain differently
Her entering

steps.confusionAlert: It is רב, the one who disagrees with רב אסי, who defends him here. He is not changing his own view. He is only showing that this proof does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: This source about the חופה does not decide the argument between רב and רב אסי, because the handing over can count as the חופה. A later ברייתא does decide it, against רב אסי (step 16).

phrases.english: רב said to them:
Didn't I tell you
not to go after something that can be turned the other way?!
phrases.notes: He means: don't try to refute someone from a source that can easily be read the opposite way.

phrases.english: He can answer you:
Her handing over, that is her entering the חופה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לְכוּ לָא תֵּיזְלוּ בָּתַר אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Entering the חופה' means only the actual חופה, which would go against רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Entering the חופה' can include the handing over, so the source does not disprove רב אסי.

steps.title: שמואל: The handing over counts only for inheritance
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that after the handing over, the husband gets only one right: he inherits her if she dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the handing over moves her to the husband only for her inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another opinion to the list. שמואל gives the handing over the smallest effect so far: it only lets the husband inherit her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the handing over counts for everything except תרומה. רב אסי said it counts even for תרומה. שמואל is much narrower. In his view the handing over gives the husband only the right to inherit her property if she dies.

keyTerms.meaning: Her inheritance. Here it means the husband inherits her property if she dies.
The handing over of the bride by her father to the husband's messengers.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: for her inheritance.
phrases.notes: He means the handing over moves her to the husband only for this: if she dies, he inherits her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion, narrower than רב and רב אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The handing over works only for the husband's right to inherit her.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The handing over counts for her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the handing over moves her to the husband with regard to her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the handing over counts for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion is added. ריש לקיש says the handing over has an effect on her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not explain what he means by "her כתובה." That missing detail sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Her marriage contract, and the money promised to her in it.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: for her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth opinion. Its meaning is unclear, which leads into the next question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The handing over has an effect on her כתובה.

steps.title: If כתובה means inheritance, ריש לקיש is just repeating שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ריש לקיש means. If he means the husband inherits her, he is saying exactly what שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this "her כתובה"? If it means that if she dies he inherits her, that is the same as שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what ריש לקיש means by "כתובה." It points out that the obvious reading would make his opinion identical to שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that the husband inherits what is written in her כתובה, such as her dowry, when she dies. But שמואל already said the husband inherits her. Two separate opinions should not say the same thing, so ריש לקיש must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to define a term.
That is the same as. Used to point out that two statements match.
He inherits her.

phrases.english: Her marriage contract: what is it?
That if she dies he inherits her?
That is the same as Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions ריש לקיש's wording by comparing it with שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of ריש לקיש's word "כתובה"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כתובה means the husband inherits her, ריש לקיש adds nothing beyond שמואל.

steps.title: רבינא: Her next כתובה is a מנה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that ריש לקיש means a different law: if she marries someone else later, her new כתובה is only a מנה, like a widow from marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: he comes to say that her כתובה from another man is a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question. He explains that ריש לקיש is talking about her כתובה from a later husband, not about inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the first husband dies after the handing over and she later marries someone else. ריש לקיש says she is treated as a widow from נשואין, the stage after the wedding. So her new כתובה is a מנה and not the larger amount given to a בתולה. This is a separate law from שמואל's, so ריש לקיש is not repeating him.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred זוז. This is the כתובה amount for a woman who was already married, compared with 200 for a בתולה.
From another man, meaning a later husband.
A widow whose husband died after the wedding stage, not only after the betrothal stage.

steps.confusionAlert: Here "כתובה" does not mean what she collects from this husband. It means how much her כתובה will be when she marries someone else later.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
To say that her marriage contract from another man is a maneh.
phrases.notes: After the handing over she counts as a widow who was already married, so her next husband owes a מנה, not 200.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving ריש לקיש a new meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כתובה meant that the husband inherits her, which is the same as שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: כתובה means her later כתובה from another man is a מנה, because she counts as a widow from נשואין.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא: The handing over counts for everything, even תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא both say the handing over moves her to the husband in every way, including eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא both say: her handing over counts for everything, even for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים give the widest opinion. The handing over works for everything, even eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their view matches רב אסי and goes against רב, who said she still may not eat תרומה. Now the full range of opinions has been laid out, and the next step tests them with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them.
For everything, in every respect.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Ḥanina both say:
Her handing over is for everything, even for teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the widest opinion, agreeing with רב אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The handing over transfers her completely, even for eating תרומה.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought: when the father's side goes along, the father inherits her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא as a challenge. Its first half: if the father's side still goes along with her, or she lodges in her own courtyard, her father inherits her if she dies. The actual challenge comes at the end of the ברייתא (step 15).
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If the father went with the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers went with the husband's messengers, or she had a courtyard on the way and went in with him to sleep there, then even if her כתובה is in her husband's house, if she dies her father inherits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that it will use as a challenge. This first half lists cases where she has not been handed over, so she is still under her father and he inherits her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the משנה, the ברייתא says that if the father's side still goes along, she has not been handed over, so the father inherits her. This agrees with all the opinions, including שמואל. The part that actually challenges anyone comes at the end of the ברייתא (step 15).

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged. Used to bring an objection from a תנאי source.
The husband's messengers.
To stay overnight. Just lodging, not for the purpose of marriage.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If the father went with the husband's messengers,
or the father's messengers went
with the husband's messengers,
or she had a courtyard along the way
and she entered it with him to lodge for the night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבָּתָהּ בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: even though her marriage contract is in her husband's house,
if she dies, her father inherits her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the opinions just listed against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views that the handing over lets her eat תרומה (רב אסי, רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא). The attack itself comes in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This half only sets up the challenge. It gives the cases where she is still under her father, before the ברייתא limits the handing over to inheritance and excludes תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: once she is handed to the husband's side, he inherits her
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא gives three ways she counts as handed to the husband. In each one, if she dies, her husband inherits her, even if her dowry is still at her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father handed her to the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers handed her to the husband's messengers, or the husband had a courtyard on the way and she went in with him for the sake of marriage, then even if her dowry is still in her father's house, if she dies her husband inherits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא it started in step 13. This half covers the cases where she has already passed to the husband's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 she was still with her father's side, so her father inherits. Here she has passed to the husband's side through his messengers or his courtyard, so the husband inherits. So far the ברייתא agrees with the earlier views. The real challenge comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: handed over
the husband's messengers
courtyard
for the sake of marriage
inherits her

phrases.english: If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּסְרוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: or the father's messengers handed her over to the husband's messengers,
or he had a courtyard along the way
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband. It's his courtyard, which matters later in רב אשי's answer.

phrases.english: and she went in with him for the sake of marriage,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבָּתָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: even though her כתובה is still in her father's house,
phrases.notes: Here כתובה means the property she brings into the marriage, which hasn't reached the husband yet.

phrases.english: if she dies, her husband inherits her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that was brought as a challenge in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views that the handing over lets her eat תרומה: רב אסי (step 5) and רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא (step 12)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This half only sets up the challenge. It shows the handing over counts for inheritance, so the limit that follows stands out.

steps.title: But for תרומה she must enter the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its ruling: the handing over counts only for inheritance. For eating תרומה, she must actually enter the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? For inheriting her. But for תרומה, a woman does not eat תרומה until she enters the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by saying the handing over works only for inheritance, not for תרומה. This line is what actually challenges the views in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי, and also רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא, said the handing over moves her to the husband in every way, including תרומה. The ברייתא says clearly that for תרומה, only the חופה counts. That contradicts them directly.

keyTerms.meaning: when is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
the holy portion given to a כהן, which his household may eat
the wedding canopy, the actual entry into marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the הלכה that handing her to the husband's messengers counts for inheritance but not for תרומה.

phrases.english: When is this said?
For inheriting her.
But for תרומה,
a woman does not eat תרומה
until she enters the חופה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and reaches the line that clashes with step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי (step 5) and רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא (step 12): the handing over lets her eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says outright that for תרומה only the חופה counts, so the handing over cannot be enough.

steps.title: A full refutation of all those views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא refutes everyone who said the handing over lets her eat תרומה, and it accepts the refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of all of them! Yes, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the ברייתא defeats those views and does not try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיובתא means the challenge stands and the opinion is rejected. Repeating the word tells us the גמרא gives up on defending those views. The final rule is that a bride may eat תרומה only after the חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: a full refutation that has no answer
of all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The handing over moves her to the husband for inheritance, but she may eat תרומה only after the חופה. Any view saying otherwise is refuted.

phrases.english: A refutation of all of them!
phrases.notes: "All of them" means everyone who said the handing over is enough for her to eat תרומה: רב אסי, רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from steps 13-15 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Handing her over does not let her eat תרומה. Only entering the חופה does. The views claiming otherwise are rejected.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself about an unstated purpose
steps.stepSummary: The first half implies that going in with no stated purpose counts as for marriage. The second half implies it counts only as lodging.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult. You said: 'she went in with him to lodge.' The reason she is not married is that it was to lodge, so if nothing was said, it is for marriage. Now say the end part: 'she went in with him for the sake of marriage,' so if nothing was said, it is only to lodge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the ברייתא itself and finds two lines that seem to point in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half says that if she went in 'to lodge,' her father still inherits. That suggests a stay with no stated purpose would count as marriage. The second half says that if she went in 'for marriage,' the husband inherits. That suggests a stay with no stated purpose would not count. The two inferences clash.

keyTerms.meaning: this itself is difficult (a contradiction inside one source)
to lodge, to stay overnight
with nothing stated, plain
say the end part (of the source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge to רבי יוחנן. That question is closed. Here the גמרא is only working out the ברייתא's own wording.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: she went in with him to lodge.
phrases.notes: This is from the first half of the ברייתא (step 13), where the courtyard on the way was hers.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was to lodge,
so if nothing was said, it counts as for marriage.
Now say the end part:
she went in with him for the sake of marriage,
so if nothing was said, it counts only as lodging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the refutation to a puzzle inside the ברייתא itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא about a stay with no stated purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the first half one way and the second half the other way gives opposite rules for the same plain case.

steps.title: רב אשי: her courtyard means lodging, his courtyard means marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא is describing two different plain cases. An unstated stay in her courtyard is for lodging. An unstated stay in his courtyard is for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The ברייתא teaches two different unstated cases. In her courtyard with nothing said, it is for lodging. In his courtyard with nothing said, it is for marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the contradiction by showing that the two halves of the ברייתא are talking about different courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half was about her courtyard, and the second half about his. When nothing is said, we assume a stay at her place is just for the night, and a stay at his place is for marriage. So the two inferences describe two different plain cases and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: it teaches two different unstated cases
hers
his

steps.whatToRemember: When nothing was said, the owner of the courtyard decides it. Her courtyard means just lodging. His courtyard means marriage, so he inherits her.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
It teaches two different unstated cases.
Her courtyard with nothing said: it is to lodge.
His courtyard with nothing said: it is for marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי סְתָמֵי סְתָמֵי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: the two halves of the ברייתא deal with different courtyards.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves describe the same plain case, so their inferences contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A plain stay in her courtyard is for lodging, and a plain stay in his courtyard is for marriage. So there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Handed to the husband's messengers: punished like a married woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the father handed his daughter to the husband's messengers and she then sinned with another man, she is punished with חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If the father handed her to the husband's messengers, and she then committed adultery, she is punished with strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the father handing his daughter to the husband's messengers. This time the subject is punishment, not inheritance or תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed נערה who sins gets סקילה (stoning). A fully married woman gets חנק (strangulation). The ברייתא says that once she is handed to the husband's messengers, she is already treated like a married woman for this punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (a ברייתא is being quoted)
The husband's messengers, sent to bring her to him
She committed adultery
Strangulation, the death penalty for a married woman who sins

phrases.english: It was taught: if the father handed her over to the husband's messengers
and she committed adultery, she is punished with strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא: מָסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל וְזִינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of handing her to the husband's messengers, now for the area of punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the father hands her to the husband's messengers, adultery is punished with חנק as for a married woman, not סקילה.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק source of this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's ruling. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a girl who is only betrothed gets סקילה if she sins. She was never actually married here, so we need a source to show that handing her over changes her punishment to חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? (a request for a source)
Stoning, the punishment for a betrothed נערה who sins
A betrothed young girl

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a girl handed to the messengers gets חנק rather than סקילה.

steps.title: The source: 'in her father's house'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי בר חמא learns it from the פסוק 'to play the harlot in her father's house.' Stoning applies only while she is in her father's domain, not once he handed her to the messengers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי בר חמא said: The פסוק says 'to play the harlot in her father's house.' This excludes a case where the father handed her to the husband's messengers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי בר חמא gives the source. The פסוק about stoning says she sinned 'in her father's house,' so once she has left her father's domain, stoning no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בית אביה limit סקילה to a girl still under her father's control. Once he hands her to the husband's messengers, she is out of his house, so she falls back to the regular married-woman punishment of חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
To commit adultery in her father's house
Excluding, leaving out a case

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami bar Chama said:
The verse says: 'to play the harlot in her father's house,'
excluding where the father handed her to the husband's messengers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר חָמָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'in her father's house' limit stoning to a girl still in her father's domain, so handing her to the messengers excludes her.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק only excludes a girl who entered the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'her father's house' might exclude only a girl who already entered the חופה, not one merely handed to the messengers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: it excludes a girl who entered the חופה but had not yet been with her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי בר חמא's reading. Maybe 'in her father's house' leaves out only the girl who already entered the חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl in the חופה is more clearly out of her father's house than one walking with messengers. If the פסוק is used up on the חופה case, the messengers case would still get סקילה, and the ברייתא would have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say instead (offering another reading)
She entered the חופה
She was with her husband (the marriage was completed physically)

phrases.english: But say: it excludes a case where she entered the chuppah
but was not yet with her husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: פְּרָט שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה וְלֹא נִבְעֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי בר חמא's use of 'בית אביה' for the messengers case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could just as well be excluding the more obvious case of a girl in the חופה, leaving the messengers case still under סקילה.

steps.title: The חופה case is already written openly
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes אמי: the חופה case is stated openly in another פסוק, 'a betrothed girl,' meaning not a married one. So 'her father's house' must be teaching something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: אמי told me, the חופה case is written openly: 'If there is a young girl, a virgin, betrothed to a man.' 'Young girl' and not a grown woman; 'virgin' and not one who had relations; 'betrothed' and not married.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge using what אמי told him. Another פסוק already excludes the girl who entered the חופה, so we do not need 'her father's house' for that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק narrows who gets סקילה. נערה excludes a בוגרת, בתולה excludes a בעולה, and מאורשה excludes a נשואה. Since the חופה case is covered here, 'her father's house' is left free to teach the messengers case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written openly, stated directly
A girl past the age of נערות (a grown woman)
A woman who is no longer a virgin
Betrothed (after קידושין, before נישואין)
Married

phrases.english: Rava said: Ami told me,
phrases.notes: This is the same רבי אמי בר חמא from before, explaining his own reading.

phrases.english: the chuppah case is written openly:
'If there is a young girl, a virgin, betrothed to a man.'
'Young girl' and not a grown woman;
'virgin' and not one who has had relations;
'betrothed' and not married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲמַר לִי אַמֵּי, חוּפָּה בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the alternate case already has its own explicit source, so the original derivation stands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In her father's house' might be needed to exclude the girl who entered the חופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חופה case is excluded by 'מאורשה, and not נשואה,' so 'בית אביה' teaches the messengers case.

steps.title: Proving that 'married' here means entered the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that 'not married' cannot mean fully married, because 'not one who had relations' already covers that. It must mean a girl who entered the חופה but was not yet with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'married'? If you say truly married, that is the same as 'virgin and not one who had relations'! Rather, does it not mean she entered the חופה but was not yet with her husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's answer. It shows that the word 'married' in the פסוק must refer to the חופה case, so that case really is written openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fully married woman has already been with her husband, so she is already excluded by 'virgin and not בעולה.' For 'not married' to add anything, it must mean a girl who entered the חופה while still a virgin. So that case is covered, and 'her father's house' teaches the messengers case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asking for the meaning of a word)
If you will say (testing one possibility)
Truly, in the full sense
That is the same as (it would just repeat)
Rather, is it not so that (bringing the only remaining option)

steps.whatToRemember: A girl handed to the husband's messengers who sins gets חנק, learned from 'in her father's house.' A girl who entered the חופה is excluded separately by 'betrothed, and not married.'

phrases.english: What is meant by 'married'?
If you say truly married,
that is the same as 'virgin' and not one who had relations!
Rather, is it not a girl who entered the chuppah
but was not yet with her husband?
phrases.notes: So the חופה case is already covered, and 'her father's house' can teach the messengers case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the key claim inside רבא's answer, that the חופה case is written openly.
steps.raayaObject: That 'מאורשה, and not נשואה' refers to a girl who entered the חופה but was not yet with her husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Since 'בתולה, and not בעולה' already excludes a fully married woman, 'נשואה' must mean something new: חופה without ביאה.
